subject: PolarBeam renewal — staged discount & onboarding credit proposal
messages:
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Alex Li <alex.li@polarbeam.io>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PolarBeam renewal discussion — early sketch

Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation I pulled together a quick sketch of options that would support PolarBeam's plan to increase inference capacity while keeping near-term unit economics predictable for your finance team. High level proposal below; attached is a short spreadsheet with commit ladder examples and a separate PDF with talking points we can share with procurement.

Key ask from your side: 2x committed peak capacity over current baseline, preferred 12-month term, and a short onboarding credit to offset migration work.

Proposed commercial sketch (subject to term/legal review):
- 12-month primary term with 3-tier commit ladder (Base / Growth / Peak) tied to monthly vGPU-hour usage.
- Initial discount banding: 18% off list at Base commit, stepping to 28% at Peak commit reached.
- Onboarding credit: one-time $60k credit applied against first two invoices to defray migration and integration validation.
- 6-month price hold on the contracted model variant(s) for delivered throughput; subsequent months transition to market-indexed pricing with a cap.

Operational notes:
- Redwood Dedicated will reserve capacity that maps to your projected monthly peaks; autoscale bursts allowed up to 1.5x for short spikes (overage billed at pay-as-you-go rates).
- We can instrument per-route latency guards and token-level cost dashboards during onboarding so you can validate cost/latency tradeoffs.

Attachments: 20271025-polarbeam-renewal-proposal.pdf, polarbeam-commit-ladder.xlsx

Next steps: if this direction looks promising, I can share a formal term sheet and loop legal/finance for a redline. Would you be able to share an updated expected monthly vGPU-hour profile for Q4–Q1 so we can finalize tiers?

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0128


From: Alex Li <alex.li@polarbeam.io>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Jordan Mayer <jordan.mayer@polarbeam.io>, Procurement Team <procurement@polarbeam.io>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 10:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PolarBeam renewal discussion — early sketch

Sergio —

Appreciate the quick follow. The sketch looks sensible and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifying points from procurement/finance:

1) We need a 9–12 month guaranteed price hold on the model family we sign for. Six months would be tight for our forecast process.
2) The onboarding credit is helpful — can it be applied as or converted into a usage credit instead of invoice credit? That helps our month-to-month runway.
3) For the commit ladder, we need a clear overage protection (soft cap) — can you add a stepped cap where overage rates escalate but are capped at a fixed multiplier?

I'll loop Jordan Mayer (engineering lead) to provide expected monthly vGPU-hours for Q4 and Q1. Procurement (procurement@polarbeam.io) will want the formal term sheet for redline.

If you can push a version that extends the price hold to 9 months and provides an option for the $60k to be applied as a usage credit, that will move this forward faster.

Regards,
Alex Li
Head of Platform Engineering | PolarBeam
alex.li@polarbeam.io

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal — PolarBeam asks (price hold + usage credit + stepped overage cap)

Team —

Recap: PolarBeam asked for:
- Extend price hold to 9 months (was asking to move from 6 -> 9)
- Convert onboarding $60k invoice credit to usage credit (applied against token/vGPU usage until exhausted)
- Add stepped overage cap (soft cap with fixed multiplier tiers)
- They plan to double committed peak capacity; expect to be live in ~8 weeks after signature.

Options I recommend to keep deal economics intact while addressing risk:
1) Term / price hold: offer 9-month hold but require a 12-month minimum term and a 20% minimum commitment floor (no rollback below Base commit).
2) Onboarding credit: allow conversion to a usage credit but amortize it over first 3 months of billed usage and require a minimal onboarding acceptance checklist sign-off to prevent misuse.
3) Overage protection: accept stepped cap — e.g., 1.25x for month 1–2, 1.5x for months 3–6; any sustained usage beyond 1.5x triggers review and optional temporary capacity top-up pricing. Overages billed at pre-agreed multipliers (1.15x / 1.35x / 1.5x).

Questions for finance/legal:
- Can we build the usage-credit construct so it shows as a contra-revenue line (not cash reduction)?
- Any concerns on a 9-month hold from pricing and indexation perspective?

I can share a marked-up term sheet if we agree to this path. Requesting Marissa + Priyom sign-off so I can send to procurement this week.

Thanks,
Sergio

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal — PolarBeam asks (price hold + usage credit + stepped overage cap)

Sergio —

Thanks for the framing. I agree with the approach with two modifications:

- Approve 9-month price hold conditional on a 12-month term and a 10% revenue-protection clause (if they underutilize below the Base commitment for more than two consecutive months we trigger a recalibration).
- Approve conversion of onboarding credit to usage credit but limit conversion to 75% convertible (i.e., $45k usage credit + $15k invoice credit) — this protects cash recognition.

Priyom: please confirm whether the usage-credit accounting treatment as contra-revenue is acceptable; if not we should default to invoice credit and be explicit in the term sheet.

Assuming finance confirms the credit treatment, Sergio, please finalize the term sheet and include the stepped overage cap language you suggested. Keep legal on the loop for a quick redline.

-Marissa
VP Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
